content.title: Boston Marathon early weather forecast
content.text: April 10, 2026, 4:03 a.m. ETSpring is finally in the air.That only means one thing: get those Nike, Adidas and Puma running shoes out of the closet.The 130th running of the Boston Marathon is set to take place on Monday, April 20. The event, established in 1897, is the world's oldest marathon which requires qualifying times based on age and gender. Runners begin at Hopkinton and end with a sprint on Boylston Street.There are plenty of obstacles to endure in the downhill 26.2-mile race. Some include Heartbreak Hill, several different flat stretches on the course and the Newton Hills. Toward the end, the scenery of the Wellesley tunnel and Copley Square catches the eyes of the runners.Now all that's left for the 30,000-plus runners to ponder about is the upcoming forecast.How many times has it snowed during the Boston Marathon?Over the years, the Boston Marathon have been plagued with unusual weather conditions, ranging from snow to mid-summer heat. Five times — 1907, 1908, 1925, 1961 and 1967 — snowflakes sprinkled down on runners. Wind swept rains also soaked runners in 1970, 2007, 2015 and 2018.What's the hottest Boston Marathon temperature?Then there's the heat factor.Extreme hot temperatures came into play during the 1907 marathon (100 degrees), the 1976 marathon (96 degrees) and the 2004 and 2012 marathons where temps reached as high as 87 degrees. In 1927, the mercury rose to 94 degrees, which freshly paved roads along the way melted under the runners' feet.With the race just under 10 days away, what are forecasters predicting for runners?Early weather forecast for 2026 Boston MarathonAs of right now, according to the Farmer's Almanac, forecasters are predicting pleasant and mild conditions with temps ranging between 55-60 degrees with manageable winds. There is a slight chance of precipitation.But of course, this is New England and the weather changes from time to time.According to forecasters from the WCVB 5 Boston StormTeam, in 1939 when runners began the race in the darkness due to a storm and a partial solar eclipse. In 2010, a volcanic eruption in Iceland disrupted travel and cause many runners to miss the marathon.So, stay tuned as we get closer to the running of the 130th Boston Marathon.Herald News and Taunton Gazette sports editor Steven Sanchez can be reached at ssanchez@heraldnews.com.
